title: Istanbul Ferries Cancelled by Wind or Fog? How to Check and Plan B
excerpt: When lodos or fog stops Şehir Hatları, İDO or BUDO, here is how to read the weather warning, confirm cancellations with the operator, and get across the Bosphorus or to the islands, Yalova and Bursa another way.

body.text: Istanbul’s ferries are the most pleasant way to cross the water, and the first service to stop when a strong wind hits the Sea of Marmara. On 13 November 2026, for example, [Türkiye Gazetesi reported](https://www.turkiyegazetesi.com.tr/haberler/vapur-seferleri-iptal-mi-son-dakika-13-kasim-sehir-hatlari-ido-budo-iptal-seferler-li-1829000) that Şehir Hatları cancelled Princes’ Islands services and the Bostancı–Moda–Karaköy–Kabataş line because of bad weather as a lodos (southwesterly) storm hit. İDO cancelled morning Yenikapı–Yalova, Bandırma and Bursa sea-bus trips, and BUDO cancelled 10 trips on its Mudanya, Armutlu and Kabataş routes. This guide is a decision plan for days like that. For the basics of Istanbulkart, metro and tram, see our [Istanbul public transport guide](/blog/istanbul-public-transport-tourist-guide).
Step 1: read the weather warning the evening before

The Turkish State Meteorological Service (MGM, mgm.gov.tr) issues colour-coded warnings. Before the 13 November storm, [Takvim reported](https://www.takvim.com.tr/meteoroloji/2026/11/12/meteorolojiden-11-ile-sari-kodlu-uyari-istanbulda-90-km-hizla-firtina) a yellow warning from the meteorological service for Istanbul and ten other provinces, including Bursa, Yalova, Kocaeli and Çanakkale. Citing the Istanbul Governor’s Office, it said winds of 60–90 km/h were expected from Friday morning, with brief spells of strong storm. [Milli Gazete](https://milligazete.com.tr/meteoroloji-marmarayi-uyardi-firtina-12-kasimda-basliyor) reported that MGM issued its strong-wind and storm warning for the Marmara region on 11 November: south and southwesterly winds from Thursday, 50–75 km/h from Friday morning, and the storm expected to ease from Saturday evening. A meteorologist quoted by Takvim warned that ferry cancellations were possible across the Sea of Marmara, especially in the afternoon, and the MGM sea forecast cited in the same report gave waves of 1–2 m, reaching 2.5 m in places.
The practical lesson: when a wind warning covers Istanbul, plan the day as if the ferry might not run. When you read a warning, note four things:

items: The colour and the provinces covered (Istanbul alone, or also Yalova, Bursa and Balıkesir for longer sea routes).
Wind direction and speed: lodos is the southwesterly wind, poyraz the northeasterly one.
The time window, including when the wind is expected to ease.
Whether the forecast mentions sea transport or wave height.

body.text: Step 2: confirm with the operator, not the pier

Each operator announces its own cancellations, and they do not all stop together. On 5 November, [Milli Gazete](https://www.milligazete.com.tr/5-kasim-vapur-seferlerinde-son-durum-ido-bandirma-seferi-iptal-edildi-sehir-hatlari-ve-budo-calisiyor-mu) noted that İDO had cancelled Bandırma trips, while no new general cancellation appeared on Şehir Hatları’s page and BUDO listed no new cancellations. It pointed readers to sehirhatlari.istanbul, ido.com.tr and budo.burulas.com.tr, which has an online schedule lookup. Turyol and Dentur are separate private operators, so check their own channels. The 13 November reports we read did not cover them.

items: Check the operator for each leg of your trip, not just the first one.

Look for the wording. On 13 November Şehir Hatları cancelled services “until a further announcement”, so a morning cancellation does not tell you when service will resume. Check again before your return leg.
Some lines are rerouted rather than cancelled: the same day, the Aşiyan–Anadolu Hisarı–Küçüksu ring and Aşiyan–Üsküdar services were rerouted.

Read times carefully. [Milliyet’s list](https://www.milliyet.com.tr/bilgi-rehberi/ido-iptal-seferler-13-kasim-cuma-istanbul-deniz-otobusleri-ido-iptal-olan-seferleri-duyurdu-7699734) of İDO cancellations was trip-specific (for example the 07:45 Bandırma–Yenikapı–Kadıköy and 09:05 Kabataş–Kadıköy–Yenikapı–Armutlu–Bursa), so a later sailing may run, or may be cancelled later.

body.text: Which routes went first on recent windy days

We have no long-term data on which lines stop first, so treat this as a pattern from two recent days, not a rule. On 5 November only İDO’s Bandırma sailings were reported cancelled. On 13 November the cancellations were concentrated on the longer crossings: the Princes’ Islands, Yalova, Armutlu, Mudanya/Bursa and Bandırma. Inner-city Bosphorus services were partly affected (Bostancı–Moda–Karaköy–Kabataş) and partly rerouted. If your day depends on an islands or Marmara crossing, it is the most fragile part of the plan.
Plan B across the Bosphorus: rail and road

Crossing between Europe and Asia does not depend on ferries. Marmaray runs under the Bosphorus by rail, and the bridges carry buses and the metrobus. When the 15 Temmuz Şehitler Bridge was closed to traffic for the Istanbul Marathon on 1 November, [İETT announced](https://iett.istanbul/Announcement/Detail/3347) that the metrobus would not run between Zincirlikuyu and Söğütlüçeşme during the race. To reach the Asian side, it pointed passengers to buses using the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge, the M2 metro to Yenikapı to change to Marmaray, or a change to Marmaray at Küçükçekmece metrobus station. That notice was about a road closure for the marathon, not about weather or ferries; we cite it only to show which land routes exist. They are the options to consider when the ferry is off.

items: Marmaray (rail tunnel): not affected by waves. It may be busier when ferry passengers switch to rail, and from hotel areas such as Sultanahmet, Karaköy or Kadıköy you will often need a transfer or a walk to reach a station.
Metrobus over the 15 Temmuz Şehitler Bridge: frequent, but it shares the weather with road traffic and is often packed at rush hour.
City buses over the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge: useful for the northern Bosphorus, but slow in heavy traffic.
Taxi: simplest with luggage, but a storm with rain usually means slower bridge traffic. Do not count on a fixed journey time.

body.text: We do not quote door-to-door times, because they depend on your hotel and the hour. Before you leave, check the route in a journey planner and add a generous margin. A ferry crossing that felt like 20 minutes on a calm day can become a transfer-heavy journey by land.
Princes’ Islands: there is no land Plan B

The islands have no bridge or tunnel to the mainland. If Şehir Hatları cancels island services, as it did on 13 November on island routes from Kabataş, Beşiktaş, Kadıköy, Bostancı and Maltepe, you cannot get there another way on public transport. Move your islands day to a calmer date and keep it flexible. If you are staying on an island, talk to your accommodation about a later departure and follow the operator’s announcements for resumption. Hiring a private boat is not a sensible workaround while a storm warning is in force.
Yalova, Bursa and Bandırma: switch to road or rethink the day

For Yalova, Mudanya/Bursa and Bandırma, the alternative is road travel by intercity coach or car. Compare coach operators’ schedules on the day and assume the road journey will differ in time and price from the sea bus. For a Bursa day trip, a cancelled morning sailing can mean the day no longer works. Postponing may be better than spending most of it on the road.

If you already hold a sea-bus ticket, ask the operator through its official channels what happens to it. We could not verify a published refund or rebooking rule for weather cancellations, so do not assume an automatic refund.
Buffers for tours and flights

According to the meteorologist [quoted by Takvim](https://www.takvim.com.tr/meteoroloji/2026/11/12/meteorolojiden-11-ile-sari-kodlu-uyari-istanbulda-90-km-hizla-firtina), strong winds mainly lengthen intervals between take-offs and landings, so the main effect on flights is longer waits and delays rather than cancellations. Plan with that in mind:

items: Do not schedule an islands, Yalova or Bursa trip on the day before an international flight; put it early in the trip so it can move.
Choose tours with a clear weather policy, and ask how they handle a cancelled sailing before you pay.
Reach the airport by land. Do not build a ferry leg into your airport transfer on a warning day.
Check MGM and the operator again the evening before and on the morning of travel.

body.text: Fog days

Fog can also delay or stop sailings. The recent disruptions in our sources were caused by wind, so we cannot say which lines are usually affected by fog. The method is the same: check the operator’s announcements for each leg and keep Marmaray or a bridge route as your fallback. If your trip is long enough, our [three-, five- and seven-day Istanbul itinerary](/blog/istanbul-itinerary-3-5-7-days) shows how to keep a flexible day in reserve. For more on cold-season travel, see [Türkiye in winter](/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide).

seo.intent: Find out whether Istanbul ferries and sea buses are cancelled because of wind or fog, where to confirm it, and how to cross the Bosphorus or reach the Princes’ Islands, Yalova or Bursa instead.
seo.uniqueValue: A weather-day decision plan: how to read an MGM warning, which operator page to check for each leg, a land/rail Plan B across the Bosphorus with honest trade-offs, and separate advice for the islands (no land option) and Yalova/Bursa, drawn from the 5 and 13 November 2026 cancellations.

quality.reviewNotes: EN master. Independent agent review on 2026-11-13: EN claims fact-checked against the six listed sources, all opened (Türkiye Gazetesi and Milliyet 13 Nov cancellation lists, Milli Gazete 5 Nov status and 11 Nov MGM warning report, Takvim warning report, İETT marathon announcement 3347); corrected wind-speed attribution (60–90 km/h via Istanbul Governor’s Office, MGM 50–75 km/h), wave-height attribution, the 5 Nov pattern (only İDO Bandırma), the İETT context (marathon road closure, not a weather notice) and source titles. DE, zh-CN, KO and ES versions reviewed against EN by the same agent. No human or native-speaker review. Operator sites and mgm.gov.tr not opened directly; no times, fares or refund rules stated; Turyol/Dentur not covered by sources.
